description: Phase 2: Add sort_order column to artist_show_assignments, add telegram_preview_message_id / telegram_video1_message_id / telegram_video2_message_id / telegram_artist_preview_sent_at columns to artists table, update Artist model struct.

steps.task: Add `sort_order` column to `artist_show_assignments` in db.rs init_db(). Call `add_column_if_missing(pool, "artist_show_assignments", "sort_order", "INTEGER DEFAULT 0")` after the table creation. This column controls the order in which artists are scheduled for Instagram preview posting (day 1 → sort_order 0, day 2 → sort_order 1, etc.).

decisions: INTEGER DEFAULT 0 — existing assignments get sort_order=0, alphabetical name fallback preserves current behavior
learnings: artist_show_assignments table is at lines 155-163 of db.rs
add_column_if_missing is at lines 5-28 of db.rs
knowledge.notes: Inserted after .execute(pool).await? for the CREATE TABLE, before the trigger

steps.task: Update all queries that fetch artists for a show to use `ORDER BY asa.sort_order, a.name COLLATE NOCASE` instead of just `ORDER BY a.name`. Two locations: (1) telegram.rs line 453 and (2) api.rs line 2653. Ensure the SELECT also includes `asa.sort_order` in the column list if needed.

decisions: Primary sort by sort_order, secondary by name — preserves alphabetical order for same sort_order values
learnings: api.rs has 4 ORDER BY locations: lines 1503, 1575, 1661, 2651
Line 1661 is for available (unassigned) artists — no asa join, left as ORDER BY a.name COLLATE NOCASE

steps.task: Add four new columns to the `artists` table in db.rs init_db() via add_column_if_missing: (1) `telegram_preview_message_id INTEGER` — stores the Telegram message ID of the main preview photo so it can be edited in-place, (2) `telegram_video1_message_id INTEGER` — stores message ID of track 1 video reply, (3) `telegram_video2_message_id INTEGER` — stores message ID of track 2 video reply, (4) `telegram_artist_preview_sent_at TEXT` — ISO timestamp of when preview was auto-sent by scheduler.

decisions: Use TEXT for timestamp (SQLite convention with datetime('now'))
Use INTEGER for message IDs (Telegram message IDs are i64)
learnings: Placed after track1_video_key/track2_video_key migrations with a Telegram preview section comment
knowledge.notes: Place after existing add_column_if_missing calls for the artists table

steps.task: Add the four new fields to the `Artist` struct in models.rs: `pub telegram_preview_message_id: Option<i64>`, `pub telegram_video1_message_id: Option<i64>`, `pub telegram_video2_message_id: Option<i64>`, `pub telegram_artist_preview_sent_at: Option<String>`. These must match the DB column names exactly for sqlx::FromRow derivation.

decisions: Option types since columns are nullable (no NOT NULL constraint)
sqlx::FromRow derives column mapping automatically by field name
learnings: Artist struct is in models.rs, has fields like instagram_posted_at, track1_video_key etc.
All existing Option<String> fields use Option<String> not Option<chrono::NaiveDateTime>
Placed between instagram_posted_at and status with a Telegram preview section comment
knowledge.notes: Place after existing telegram_preview_sent_at or at the end before status/created_at/updated_at

steps.task: Run `cargo check` from source/backend/ to verify Phase 2 compiles. Fix any sqlx or struct field mismatch errors.

learnings: cargo check passes with 15 warnings (same as after Phase 1 — no new warnings)
knowledge.notes: Common issue: sqlx queries with SELECT * may need recompilation after adding columns if using compile-time checked queries. This project uses runtime queries (query_as with string SQL) so it should be fine.
